question: What is said to be done when the force of 2 Newtons moves an object of 2 grams, 2 metres in the direction of the force?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Work.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Work is defined as the **energy** that is** applied to or removed **from an object by applying** force along a displacement.**
 
• Work equals the **product of the force's magnitude **and the** distance traveled for a constant force **directed in the same direction as the motion.
 
 
• **W = (F cos θ) d = F. d**
 
• Where, **W** is the **work done **by the force.
 
• **F** represents the** force**, while** d** is the **force-caused displacement.**
 
• **θ** is the** angle between** the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
 
 
• The dimension of work is** [ML²T⁻²].**
 
• The** joule (J)** is the **SI unit of work**.
 
• It is the** amount of force** needed to **move an object one Newton** through a **given space of time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement:**

 
 
• It is a vector whose length is the** shortest distance from the initial to the final position **of a point.
 
 
 
• **Velocity:**
 
 
• It is a vector quantity that refers to** "the rate at which an object changes its position."**
 
 
 
• **Gravity**:
 
 
• It is the force by which a** planet or other body draws objects** toward its **center.**
